phase.description: Establish safe, fail-closed incremental validation and content-addressed caching while retaining authoritative full validation.
acceptanceCriteria: Every cacheable validation result is keyed by content fingerprints covering all identified validation-relevant inputs, declared dependencies, applicable policy/configuration, and validator/tool compatibility information.
A missing, unverifiable, incomplete, stale, corrupted, incompatible, or dependency-unsafe cache state never yields a reused pass; it fails closed to full validation or a blocking result.
Automated tests demonstrate invalidation when each material cache-key input changes and demonstrate that unknown dependency safety cannot produce a cache hit.
For an approved representative corpus of eligible changes, incremental and full validation yield equivalent governance/validation outcomes.
Full validation remains invocable and authoritative, with no removed checks or reduced gate enforcement.
Tests demonstrate that existing owner gates remain required and cannot be satisfied, bypassed, or altered merely through cache reuse.
Implementation and tests record cache eligibility exclusions for validators or gates whose dependency safety cannot be proven.
requiredValidators: targeted unit and integration tests for fingerprinting, cache addressing, invalidation, corruption handling, and fail-closed behavior
incremental-versus-full validation equivalence suite on representative fixtures
static analysis, formatting, and repository-required checks
requiredReviews: maintainer/architecture review of dependency model and cache-key completeness
security/reliability review of cache integrity, invalidation, and fail-closed handling
governance review confirming owner-gate semantics are unchanged
requiredOwnerGates: Owner approval is required before any production cache sharing, production rollout, or change to mandatory command workflows.
Any validator or gate without demonstrable dependency-safe cache eligibility remains full-validation-only.
Existing owner gates remain in force and are not delegated, bypassed, or satisfied by this proposed work.
